hero.label: About Us
hero.heading: Shaping Africa's Climate Future
hero.para1: In 2022, our climate team at GAYO took a bold step: we named and challenged the glaring inequalities in the rapidly evolving field of climate technologies. We saw firsthand how African voices were being sidelined in critical global dialogues; not because of lack of will, but due to structural barriers and persistent knowledge gaps.
hero.para2: In response, we set out to build something fundamentally different: safe, accessible spaces where African voices can lead climate discussions, allowing local stakeholders to shape their own positions on Frontier Climate Technologies.
hero.para3: Now, after three years of dedicated work, we are transitioning from GAYO to become Emerging Climate Frontiers (ECF); an independent organization ready to scale our impact, deepen our research, and meet the growing demand across the continent.

mission.title: Our Mission
mission.body: ECF Africa creates the conditions for African countries to build their own understanding of Frontier Climate Technologies (FCTs), specifically Solar Radiation Management, Carbon Dioxide Removal, and AI for climate governance, and to develop the structures that strengthen continental research capacity and enable confident engagement in global governance processes. We work with early-career researchers, established scientists, policymakers, academic institutions, and civil society organizations rooted in Africa's diverse climate geographies, ensuring that frontier climate technology science reflects the realities of the communities most exposed to its consequences, not just the interests of those who currently have the resources to dictate the science or governance.

northStar.title: Our Vision
northStar.body: ECF Africa envisions a continental research and governance landscape for frontier climate technologies where African institutions are active contributors to the science, and where African policymakers can engage substantively in global governance decisions rather than ratifying choices made elsewhere.
northStar.para1: ECF Africa envisions a continental research and governance landscape for frontier climate technologies where African institutions are active contributors to the science, and where African policymakers can engage substantively in global governance decisions rather than ratifying choices made elsewhere.
northStar.para2: Africa is not a single climate. From the Sahel to the Congo Basin, the Horn to the southern African plateau, and the Indian Ocean small island states, every region faces distinct realities, and the consequences of any FCT deployment, whether to radiative balance, carbon sequestration, or AI-driven climate modelling, will land differently in each. That makes a place-based approach essential: African scientists who understand local climate dynamics, policymakers who can engage seriously with governance proposals on terms grounded in regional realities, and institutions with the capacity to sustain this work over decades. ECF exists to build that capacity where it is missing across the continent and connect African researchers and institutions to global networks where it exists.

howWeWork.heading: How We Work
howWeWork.description: Our approach to building African climate technology leadership.

capacity.title: Research Capacity Building
capacity.description: ECF designs and facilitates place-based training programs, fellowships, and research partnerships that build scientific expertise in SRM, CDR, and AI for climate governance in regions where such capacity is currently limited. We work with institutions over multi-year periods. The measure of success is whether, two years after a program ends, the institution is still doing the work.

policy.title: Policy Engagement
policy.description: ECF translates FCT science into forms that policymakers can use: policy briefs, governance simulation exercises, and direct engagement with government ministries and science advisory bodies. We also train researchers to communicate their work to non-specialist audiences, because the gap between the science and the policy conversation is often more about communication than content.

network.title: Network Building
network.description: ECF connects researchers, institutions, and policymakers across regions working on SRM, CDR, and AI. FCT governance is a global problem that requires a global conversation. We host convenings, maintain collaborative platforms, and facilitate ongoing exchange between partner institutions so that relationships formed through ECF programs continue beyond the programs themselves.

movement.title: Movement Building for Climate Justice
movement.description: We ignite and sustain a vibrant, globally-rooted movement to advance equitable and contextually relevant FCTs, uniting diverse voices from youth, marginalized communities, and policymakers. By organizing public dialogues and advocacy initiatives, we empower communities to influence local and global climate governance. Our efforts cultivate a shared vision for climate justice across SRM, CDR, and AI, driving transformative change and ensuring these technologies serve the ecological and social realities of the communities most at stake.

outro.heading: The Journey Continues
outro.description: Building a future where Africa leads climate technology.

founded.title: ECF Founded Within GAYO
founded.description: Our climate team at GAYO took a bold step to challenge inequalities in the climate technology field and create spaces for African leadership.

geoDialogue.title: Africa's First Geoengineering Dialogue Launched
geoDialogue.description: Launched the continent's first open virtual dialogue on geoengineering to discuss these technologies from distinctly African perspectives.

srmSession.title: First Public SRM Session at UN Climate Conference
srmSession.description: Organized the first-ever public session on Solar Radiation Management at a UN Climate Conference, demonstrating Africa's readiness to engage on the global stage.

baseline.title: Baseline Knowledge Assessment Published
baseline.description: Published a comprehensive baseline knowledge assessment on climate interventions, highlighting gaps between the Global South and Global North.

partnerships.title: Institutional Partnerships Established
partnerships.description: Partnered with CSIR in Ghana and South Africa, and Environmental Protection Agencies (EPA) to build capacity within national research and regulatory bodies.

acifer.title: ACIFER Fellowship Launched
acifer.description: Pioneered the African Climate Intervention Fellowship for Early-Career Researchers in partnership with the African Climate Intervention Research Hub.

carbonAccounting.title: Carbon Accounting Training Program Delivered
carbonAccounting.description: Trained 20 professionals in carbon accounting and decarbonization, with 10 strategically placed in industries and public institutions.

shortCourses.title: University Short Courses Initiated
shortCourses.description: Partnered with universities in Ghana, Kenya, and South Africa to launch dedicated short courses on climate interventions.

transition.title: Transition to Independent Organization
transition.description: Began transitioning from GAYO to become Emerging Climate Frontiers (ECF), an independent organization ready to scale impact across the continent.

team.heading: Meet Our Team
team.description: A dedicated team of African climate advocates, researchers, and organizers.

ernest.bio: Member of the European Union Youth Sounding Board, former Regional Focal Point & Education and Capacity Building officer of the Youth Climate Councils. Co-author of the Ghana National Youth Climate Statement 2022 & 2023.

vida.bio: Gender and climate science advocate. African Youth Negotiator Fellow and a sole female youth negotiator for the Africa Group of Negotiators at the first Global Stocktake (GST) at COP28, amplifying youth and gender perspectives in high-level climate diplomacy.

elijah.bio: Former Head of Research at the Policy Action Initiative, with publications on food security and agro-ecological practices in Kenya. Currently exploring how Solar Radiation Modification (SRM) could impact agriculture and food systems in East Africa.

taylen.bio: Grassroots organiser and environmental activist. Africa Focal Point for UNEP Major Group on Children and Youth. Founded Zero Waste Durban and led the bridging of grassroots climate and environmental solutions with national and international policy and law.

kwesi.bio: A climate research scientist with experience in climate & solar geoengineering impact modeling to understand its potential benefits and broad risks. Kwesi has consulted for UNEP through the Ghana National Adaptation Project, World Meteorological Organization, The World Academy of Sciences, and ICLEI - Local Governments for Sustainability.

siisi.bio: A core member of Ghana's first Climate Literacy Portal, expanding access to climate knowledge nationwide. With the Climate and Development Knowledge Network (CDKN), he has designed innovative climate literacy games that make complex issues engaging and accessible.
